Taiwan’s Industrial Intermediate Prod Sector Sees Stable Growth Amid Steady Global Demand

Taipei—Taiwan’s Industrial Intermediate Prod sector reported steady growth in the latest quarter, reflecting sustained demand from key export markets and a robust domestic manufacturing environment. According to data released Thursday by the Taiwan Industrial Economics Institute (TIEI), industry revenue reached NT$184.7 billion for the first quarter, representing a 4.2% increase year-on-year.

Industry leaders pointed to stable order flows from Southeast Asia and North America as primary drivers of the positive results. “Our clients in electronics and automotive supply chains have maintained a consistent pace of orders,” said Lin Chia-hung, Chief Financial Officer of ZhenTech Materials, one of the sector’s major players. “While year-on-year growth is moderate, the quality of demand remains solid, and backlogs are healthy.”

Gross margins for the sector averaged 21.8%, up from 20.5% a year earlier, supported by improvements in production efficiencies and a gradual easing of input costs. TIEI analysts attributed the margin expansion to optimization efforts across the industry, including automation upgrades and supply chain consolidation.

“Taiwan’s intermediate product manufacturers have continued to adapt to the changing landscape, investing in smarter processes and diversifying their customer base,” said Esther Wang, senior industry analyst at TIEI. “This has helped buffer the sector against some of the volatility seen in other manufacturing industries across the region.”

Exports accounted for more than 62% of total sector revenue, with shipments to ASEAN countries and the United States outpacing those to Europe. Domestic demand remained stable, bolstered by ongoing infrastructure and technology projects.

The Taiwan Industrial Intermediate Products Association (TIIPA) expressed cautious optimism about the outlook. “Global demand remains resilient, particularly in specialized materials and components for electronics and machinery,” said TIIPA chairman Chen Wei-lung. “We expect orderly market conditions to persist, given the absence of major supply chain disruptions or policy shifts.”

Employment in the sector held steady, with the number of workers employed in intermediate goods manufacturing rising marginally to 71,300. Industry observers note that ongoing investments in training and process improvement are likely to support further incremental growth in the coming quarters.
